title: What Blockle is
text: Blockle is a non-custodial multi-chain wallet (browser extension, web PWA at blockle.org/wallet, Flutter mobile app, and a Python/Qt desktop wallet). It holds keys for BLOCK (its own post-quantum ML-DSA chain) plus EVM chains and Solana. All four wallets share one agent engine: a conversational assistant, a persistent trading-bot platform, and a non-custodial exchange/AMM. The user's keys and seed never leave their device.

title: Custody and signing never depend on the LLM
text: The LLM only talks: it proposes actions in plain language. It can never move funds. Every value-moving action is built, signed and broadcast by the wallet itself and must pass one non-bypassable gate: prepare -> per-session USD cap check -> explicit human confirmation -> commit. The assistant cannot weaken, skip, or auto-approve that gate, and must never ask for a password, seed phrase, private key, or API key.

title: Run the model on your own computer
text: You can point the wallet at a local LLM so nothing leaves your machine and there is no quota or key. Install Ollama (ollama.com), run 'ollama pull qwen2.5:3b-instruct' (or llama3.2 / a larger 8B+ model), then set the wallet's Brain to Local with base URL http://localhost:11434. LM Studio works too (http://localhost:1234, enable CORS). This is the recommended, private, free default for smart-trading chat.

title: Bring-your-own API key providers
text: Instead of a local model you can connect Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT (OpenAI), GitHub Copilot, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (base URL + model + key). The key is sealed in the encrypted vault, used only to call that provider's own API over TLS, and is never sent to any Blockle server. Choose this in the agent/Brain settings.

title: Blockle hosted brain is optional, not the default
text: Blockle runs an optional hosted agent gateway (agent.blockle.org) so you can try the assistant with nothing installed. It is keyless (you sign a one-time challenge proving your address, not a spend) and rate-limited on the free tier. In hosted mode your chat turns and a short-lived session token transit Blockle's server; no keys or seeds ever do. Prefer a Local or BYO provider for privacy and no quota.

title: Strategy: DCA (dollar-cost averaging)
text: DCA buys a fixed USD amount of an asset on a fixed interval regardless of price. Knobs: asset, quote (default USDC), usdPerBuy (default 10), intervalSec (default 86400 = daily). Pure-math planner — it emits a timed buy; the signing gate still confirms each buy.

title: Strategy: Grid
text: Grid places staggered buy/sell orders above and below a center price to harvest range-bound volatility. Knobs: market, levels (default 6), stepBps (spacing, default 50 = 0.5%), sizeUsdPerLevel (default 10), recenter. Best in sideways markets; pure-math.

title: Strategy: Arbitrage
text: Arbitrage compares the same pair across venues and trades only when the edge beats fees+gas. Knobs: pair, venues, minEdgeBps (default 30), maxNotionalUsd (default 50), gasBufferUsd (default 2), slippageBps (default 10). It never trades below the fee-aware threshold.

title: Strategy: Rebalance
text: Rebalance keeps a target portfolio mix by selling overweight assets and buying underweight ones once drift leaves a band. Knobs: targets (weights), bandBps (default 500 = 5%), baseQuote (USDC), maxTradeUsd (default 50). A rebalance is a SEQUENCE of swaps, each separately gated.

title: Strategy: Momentum (SMA crossover)
text: Momentum buys on a golden cross (fast SMA crosses above slow) and sells held on a death cross. Knobs: market, shortN (default 10), longN (default 30), tradeUsd (default 20). It skips entries whose expected move is below the round-trip fee threshold.

title: Indicator planner: RSI
text: RSI buys when oversold and sells held when overbought. Knobs: market, period (default 14), oversold (default 30), overbought (default 70), budgetUsd (default 1000), positionPct (default 100). One of the nine single-market indicator planners.

title: Indicator planner: MACD
text: MACD trades the signal-line crossover: buy when MACD crosses above its signal, sell held when it crosses below. Knobs: market, fast (12), slow (26), signalP (9), budgetUsd (1000), positionPct (100). Needs fast < slow.

title: Indicator planner: Bollinger Bands
text: Bollinger fades the bands: buy on a lower-band pierce, sell held on an upper-band pierce. Knobs: market, period (20), k (stddev multiplier, default 2), budgetUsd (1000), positionPct (100).

title: Indicator planner: Breakout (Donchian)
text: Breakout buys a new range high and sells held when price breaks the trailing range low. Knobs: market, lookback (default 20), budgetUsd (1000), positionPct (100). Trend-following.

title: Indicator planner: EMA cross
text: EMA cross follows trend: buy when the fast EMA crosses above the slow EMA, sell held on the reverse. Knobs: market, fast (10), slow (30), budgetUsd (1000), positionPct (100). Needs fast < slow.

title: Indicator planner: Momentum ROC
text: Momentum ROC buys when rate-of-change over a lookback exceeds a threshold and exits when it falls back. Knobs: market, lookback (default 10), thresholdPct (default 3), budgetUsd (1000), positionPct (100).

title: Indicator planner: Mean reversion
text: Mean reversion buys when price is a set percent below its moving average and sells when it reverts above. Knobs: market, period (20), bandPct (default 5), budgetUsd (1000), positionPct (100).

title: Indicator planner: Rebalance-hold
text: Rebalance-hold keeps a single-market target allocation, trading only when it drifts past a band. Knobs: market, targetPct (default 50), driftPct (default 10), budgetUsd (1000), positionPct (100).

title: Indicator planner: HODL
text: HODL buys once with the budget and holds — a baseline/benchmark. Knobs: market, budgetUsd (1000), positionPct (100). Useful to compare active strategies against buy-and-hold in the backtest.

title: The strategy planners are pure math, not the LLM
text: All fourteen strategies (arbitrage, dca, grid, rebalance, momentum, and the nine indicator planners rsi/macd/bollinger/breakout/emacross/momentum_roc/meanrev/rebalance_hold/hodl) are deterministic math engines. They produce identical decisions in every wallet and never call an LLM. The assistant can explain or configure them, but the planners run on their own.

title: Fee model
text: Every agent/bot trade carries a mandatory 0.05% (5 bps) agent fee as a second treasury transfer in the same gated action. Strategies are fee-aware: momentum/arbitrage and the indicator planners skip entries whose expected move is below the round-trip cost. The fee rides the same input asset and is included in the cap pre-check so a trade can never commit if trade+fee breach a cap.

title: Bot / channel caps by subscription tier
text: Live agent channels and bots are tier-gated: Free = 1 channel, paper-only (no live trading); Blockle Copilot = 3 live channels; Copilot Pro = unlimited live channels. Paper/Arena bots are always allowed. The tier is read live from the linked blockle.org account and fails closed to Free. Upgrade at blockle.org/copilot.

title: Paper by default, live needs caps + confirm
text: Bots default to paper (play-money) trading. A live value-moving channel refuses to start until it has a per-session USD spend cap (a catch-all sessionUsd that covers every asset) and a confirmation handler. A per-asset cap alone is not enough. The Arena is pure play-money for comparing strategies.

title: Backtest and USE THIS STRATEGY
text: Each strategy is backtested over about a month of real prices and ranked by result. From the ranked list you tap USE THIS STRATEGY to create a bot pre-filled with that strategy's knobs, bound to a wallet/account and a budget. You then set caps and arm it (paper or, on a paid tier, live).

title: Supported chains and tokens
text: Blockle spans its native BLOCK chain (BLOCK-20 token standard, BLOCK-721 NFTs), EVM chains (e.g. Ethereum, Base), and Solana. Common assets: BLOCK, USDC, USDT, USDB (Blockle's USD stablecoin, BLOCK-20S), WORLD, and wBLOCK (wrapped BLOCK SPL on Solana). Balances and swaps work across these via the wallet's chain adapters and the non-custodial exchange/AMM.

title: What you can ask the assistant
text: Plain-language commands route to one gated tool call or a sequence: 'send 0.1 ETH to alice.eth', 'swap 100 USDC to SOL', 'rebalance to 60/40 stables', 'what is my net worth?', 'which bot made money this week?'. Actions are confirmed per step; questions are answered only from real wallet/engine data, never invented.

title: Queries answer only from real data
text: When you ask about balances, net worth, prices, or bot P&L, the assistant runs read-only tools (net_worth, bots_pnl, get_balance, quotes) and must base every number on a tool result. If a source is unavailable it says so honestly rather than guessing. A query can never reach a value-moving tool.

title: Kill switch and isolation
text: An always-visible kill switch stops every agent channel, wipes the in-memory LLM credential, and locks the vault in one tap. Each channel is isolated: its own provider, caps, audit log, and P&L; a cap hit or kill on one never affects another. Agent actions are recorded in a hash-chained audit log.

title: Sending to names resolves to a verified address
text: When you say 'send to alice.eth' (or an SNS/address-book name), the wallet resolves it to a concrete address first and shows the resolved address; that resolved address is what gets inspected, confirmed, and sent. A name that does not resolve is a hard error — the wallet never sends to an unverified name.

title: Security suite can force a confirm
text: Before signing, the wallet inspects the transaction (scam/drainer denylist, approval-to-unknown-spender, large-share transfers). A danger-severity finding forces an explicit human confirm even inside a bot's allocation or under an auto-approve threshold, with the warnings shown in the confirm sheet. It fails closed: with no confirm path, a dangerous action is refused.
